problem: Erdos #835 (Erdos-Rosenfeld): does J(2k,k) have chromatic number k+1 for some k>2? First open case k=10: is J(20,10) properly 11-colorable?

main_result.statement: The C11-twisted ansatz for k=10 is REFUTED: there is NO proper 11-coloring of J(20,10) satisfying color(sigma(A)) = color(A) + 1 (mod 11) for the 11-cycle sigma = (1 2 ... 11) fixing 12..20.
main_result.consequence: Equivalently (by conjugacy of 11-cycles in S20, by relabeling of an 11-cycle color action to +1, and by impossibility of sigma-invariant colorings due to within-orbit edges): NO proper 11-coloring of J(20,10) admits ANY symmetry of order 11, i.e. no pair (g, pi) with g in Aut(J(20,10)) of order 11 and pi any permutation of the 11 colors such that color(gA) = pi(color(A)). In particular every AGL(1,11)-equivariant ansatz is dead a fortiori. The k=10 case itself remains OPEN in both directions.

drat_certificate.solve: kissat j20_10.cnf j20_10.drat: s UNSATISFIABLE in 297.64 s (5th independent UNSAT)
drat_certificate.note: UNSAT core touches only 0.5% of the original clauses -- a compact refutation exists; core extraction is a promising route to a human-readable mod-11 obstruction.
